what_its_for: Amifampridine is used to treat Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS), a rare disease that causes muscle weakness. It works by helping your nerves send better signals to your muscles, which can improve your strength and ability to move.
how_to_take: Take amifampridine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or split them. Try to space your doses evenly throughout the day. Take each dose at the same times every day to keep a steady amount of the medicine in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it based on how well it works and how you feel. The usual starting dose is 15 to 30 mg per day, split into 3 or 4 doses. Your doctor may increase your dose over time, but most people take no more than 80 mg per day. Never take more than 20 mg in a single dose or more than 80 mg in one day unless your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next scheduled dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once or double up to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store amifampridine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a dry place, such as a drawer or cabinet — not in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking amifampridine, as it may worsen side effects. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, especially medicines that can lower the seizure threshold, such as certain antidepressants or antipsychotics. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, because it may cause dizziness or weakness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: seizures or convulsions, severe allergic reactions (such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing), chest pain or irregular heartbeat, fainting, severe dizziness, or numbness and tingling that gets much worse. Also call your doctor if you notice unusual muscle spasms, confusion, or any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: Some people notice improvement in muscle strength within a few days to weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take several weeks to feel the full benefit. Continue taking it as prescribed even if you feel better. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness. Children: Ruzurgi is approved for patients 6 years and older. The dosing for children is based on body weight and will be determined by the doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not fully known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or passes into breast milk. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
